--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Parent is simple reciprocal with forgiveness. But overall, we can design better." / "Parent is basically Tit-for-Tat with forgiveness after consecutive defections. It got highest fitness among population. Need improve."
STRATEGY: Parent is simple reciprocal/TFT with forgiveness after consecutive defections. The trace simulates matches against Always C, Always D, TFT, Grim, and population/archive opponents. It proposes adding endgame defection, conditional forgiveness, and probing/exploitation of always-cooperative opponents.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So how can we improve parent? The main flaw of parent is forgiving against always D. We can fix that. Also, parent doesn't defect on last round. We can add that. Those are safe improvements."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates by default, retaliates after opponent defection, and forgives after 2-3 consecutive defections with low probability. The trace simulates modified variants against Always C, TFT, Always D, Grim, and slot 4, including a test-for-Always-C variant. It proposes adding last-round defection and conditioning forgiveness on opponent's overall defection rate / never-cooperated status.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent's forgiveness is a heuristic to break cycles. It's probably fine." / "Let's write the improved strategy. It will be a modified version of parent."
STRATEGY: Parent starts C, retaliates after opponent D, and forgives after consecutive defections with low probability. The trace simulates parent against Always C, TFT, Always D, random defectors, Grim, and slot 11. It changes the strategy by defecting on the last round, defecting if the opponent has never cooperated, and defecting if the opponent's defection rate is at least 80%, while keeping parent's forgiveness logic otherwise.
